meta.description: The yearly values each efficiency signal is computed from, and the fitted line for turning points.

sources.name: Blender Open Data benchmark snapshots
sources.licence: CC0 (Creative Commons Zero), stated on https://opendata.blender.org/download/ and in the LICENSE.txt shipped in each snapshot. No conditions on reuse; the site credits it anyway.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; snapshots are regenerated daily

sources.name: SPECpower_ssj2008 published results
sources.licence: SPEC Fair Use Rules (https://www.spec.org/products/fairuse), the same general rules as SPEC CPU 2017: state the source and retrieval date, name the licensee of each result, acknowledge the SPEC trademarks, compare SPEC metrics only within the same benchmark, and label derived values. The SPECpower section of those rules has not been re-read for this entry, because spec.org could not be reached from the build machine on 22 November 2026.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; SPEC publishes new results every few weeks
sources.typical_lag: results appear weeks to months after the test date

limitations: Signals describe how fast the past moved. None is a forecast.
Launch years with fewer than 3 benchmarked chips are left out of the yearly series.
The price signal uses today's prices for chips of every launch year, not launch prices.
Apple silicon is not on this page, so no gap involving Apple is measured.
